value.rationale: A constrained two-application timing problem is a motivated mathematical proxy for low-frequency water inputs. The exact global schedule has an activation threshold and a distinct amount-dependent midpoint crossing; a full classification distinguishes early and late interior schedules and gives their sensitivity. An illustrative input produces 12.79% higher cumulative response than coincident timing, a meaningful model-level difference, with no field-calibrated claim.
